title: Geological Cross-Section Layering and Cutting Visualization
prompt:
Use Three.js to implement a geological cross-section with 5 layers: each layer must have a different material color (soil, sandstone, limestone, shale, and granite), and the layers may have different thicknesses. Represent them using extruded solids (ExtrudeGeometry extruded along the cross-section) or a combination of layered Boxes.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
Use the following importmap in <head>, and import via ES Modules in <script type="module">:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
<script type="module">
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';
</script>

[Layering and Cross-Section Cutting]
(1) Exactly 5 layers; each layer must have a name and thickness (numeric values displayed in __3D_STATE__).
(2) Cut position: use a slider with id="cutPosition", with a range of 0–1 or -1–1, to move the cutting plane/clip along the cutting axis and expose the internal stratification.
(3) Clicking a layer (via raycasting) must display text such as the layer name and thickness in the element with id="layerInfo".
(4) Each layer must be independently shown/hidden: provide a toggle control for each layer, with suggested ids layerVis0 … layerVis4 (or a unified list using data-layer-index); the states must be reflected as boolean[5] in __3D_STATE__.layerVisibility.

[Rendering]
(5) OrbitControls, lighting, and a ground reference are optional.

[State Exposure (Required)]
Update window.__3D_STATE__ every frame:
  - layerCount: number (should be 5)
  - cutPosition: number
  - selectedLayer: string | null (layer name or id)
  - layerVisibility: boolean[] (length 5)
  - layers: Array<{ name: string, thickness: number, visible: boolean }>

Output a single HTML file.
